# Share link row — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for the share link row when a link needs minting, copying and revoking in one place. `link` is the required share-link model with `onCopy` and `onRevoke` carrying the actions out to the host, and `scopes` with the scope selector sets the per-recipient scope without leaving the row. There is no clipboard write inside — the copy callback fires and the host writes, so the row never touches the clipboard — and no scope model either, since minting and per-recipient scope live wherever links come from while the row renders and reports. Scope picking stays an inline picker with the picker's option contract rather than a nested surface, the link state reads through the status pill as Active, Copied or Revoked from the one registry, and revoking confirms through the overlay alert — destruction always asks first. Copy and revoke labels are props, so the row speaks the host's language.

## Native

### Features

Reach for the share link row when a link needs minting, copying and revoking in one place — the native twin under the same contract. `link` is the required share-link model with `onCopy` and `onRevoke` carrying the actions out to the host, and `scopes` with the scope selector sets the per-recipient scope without leaving the row. There is no clipboard write inside — the copy callback fires and the host writes, so the row never touches the clipboard — and no scope model either, since minting and per-recipient scope live wherever links come from while the row renders and reports. Scope picking stays an inline picker with the picker's option contract rather than a nested surface, the link state reads through the status pill as Active, Copied or Revoked from the one registry, and revoking confirms through the confirm expression — destruction always asks first. Copy and revoke labels are props, so the row speaks the host's language.
